title: Self-Hosted Model Deployment Shape Decision
summary: Choose among workstation, container or on-premises, edge, and cloud-managed model compute using workload, authority, evidence, and recovery requirements.
prerequisites: A bounded workload and prohibited-use statement
Data classification, service objectives, and recovery objectives
Named owners for model, infrastructure, security, and release decisions

sections.title: Compare responsibility, not product labels
paragraphs: A workstation can minimize network dependence and support individual experimentation, but it inherits device access, thermal, power, storage, patching, and single-machine recovery limits. A container or on-premises service can standardize runtime and shared access, while adding host, image, network, scheduler, capacity, backup, and incident ownership. An edge service can reduce round-trip latency and operate with intermittent connectivity, but must fit device memory, power, update, observability, physical-access, and rollback constraints. Cloud-managed compute can delegate hardware provisioning and some service operations while retaining model selection, authorization, data, evaluation, quota, cost, lifecycle, and recovery responsibilities.

Do not select a shape from one benchmark or a privacy slogan. Compare the same exact model, runtime contract, request distribution, data boundary, failure cases, and service objectives. A shape is viable only when the organization has authority to use the artifacts and environment, can verify the intended workload, can stop unsafe traffic, and can restore a known-good serving unit.

sections.title: Record an expiring, evidence-backed choice
paragraphs: Evaluate workload locality, disconnected operation, latency distribution, concurrency, context and output bounds, accelerator availability, energy, idle capacity, portability, isolation, staffing, support, update cadence, telemetry, cost, and recovery. Date hardware, pricing, quota, version, and lifecycle observations or link the decision to a current first-party source instead of copying volatile values into a long-lived guide.

Keep the stable service contract separate from each environment adapter. The contract identifies inputs, outputs, errors, limits, identity, evidence, and recovery; adapters hold workstation, container, edge, or cloud-specific implementation details. This makes a future move a measured adapter change instead of a rewrite of the operating promise.

code.label: Deployment shape decision record
code.code:
Task: [BOUNDED MODEL-SERVICE WORKLOAD]
Scope: [USERS, DATA, LOCATIONS, REQUEST SHAPE, AND NON-GOALS]
Permissions: [MODEL/LICENSE, DATA, DEVICE/CLOUD, NETWORK, AND RELEASE AUTHORITY]
Exact build: [MODEL REVISION + DIGEST, RUNTIME/IMAGE, ADAPTER, POLICY, AND CONFIG]
Candidates: [WORKSTATION | CONTAINER/ON-PREMISES | EDGE | CLOUD-MANAGED]
Demand: [CONTEXT, OUTPUT, CONCURRENCY, BURST, LATENCY, AVAILABILITY, AND COST]
Control boundary: [IDENTITY, NETWORK, SECRETS, TELEMETRY, UPDATE, AND SUPPORT]
Decision evidence: [QUALITY/SAFETY, LOAD, FAILURE, TCO, STAFFING, AND PORTABILITY]
Decision owner and review date: [AUTHORIZED ROLE + YYYY-MM-DD]
Verification: [REPRODUCE BUILD, REPRESENTATIVE TESTS, FAILURE TEST, AND RESTORE]
Stop conditions: [LICENSE GAP, DATA VIOLATION, CRITICAL EVAL FAILURE, UNSAFE SATURATION, OR UNOWNED RECOVERY]
Recovery: [STOP ADMISSION, RECONCILE WORK, RESTORE KNOWN-GOOD UNIT, VERIFY POSTCONDITIONS]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the bounded mission, data and authority boundaries, exact artifact and runtime identities, one comparable evaluation and load profile, failure and restore results, cost assumptions, operating owners, residual risks, selected shape, rejected alternatives, and next review date. A successful chat response is not deployment evidence.

Verify the selected shape under representative load and at least one declared failure. Stop when a legal, data, identity, critical-evaluation, capacity, or recovery gate fails. Preserve secret-free evidence, block new work, reconcile in-flight effects, restore the verified fallback, and reopen the decision when demand, hardware, pricing, quota, runtime support, or organizational ownership materially changes.

sections.title: A field guide to deployment-shape responsibility
paragraphs: A deployment shape is a responsibility boundary, not a product ranking. A workstation reduces network dependence for one operator, but its owner remains responsible for the device, thermal and power behavior, storage, patching, access, and single-machine recovery. Containers do not receive CPU or memory limits by default, so operators must configure and test limits rather than assume isolation. Docker documents these behaviors at https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/resource_constraints/ (checked 2026-09-20).

A container or on-premises service can provide a shared local service, but its owners must operate hosts, images, networks, schedulers, capacity, backups, rollouts, and incidents. Kubernetes Deployments manage desired application state and controlled updates, but they do not by themselves prove application safety, artifact identity, capacity, or successful restoration. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/ (checked 2026-09-20).

Edge deployment can reduce network round trips and support operation during intermittent connectivity, but device memory, power, physical access, observability, update, and rollback remain deployment-specific obligations. ONNX Runtime provides first-party edge and IoT deployment guidance at https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/tutorials/iot-edge/ (checked 2026-09-20). That guidance does not prove that a particular model fits a particular device.

Cloud-managed compute can delegate some hardware provisioning and infrastructure operation. The customer still needs evidence for artifact permission, data authority, identity, evaluation, quota, cost, lifecycle, outage behavior, and recovery. Microsoft describes managed-compute responsibilities at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/managed-compute-overview/ (checked 2026-09-20).

This guide uses the following course decision procedure: first test legal and data authority, then identity and access control, critical safety and quality evaluation, recovery and restoration, and capacity and service objectives. Apply preference scoring only after every hard gate passes. This ordering is a Project 42 teaching protocol, not a claim that the cited platform documentation mandates this exact sequence. PASS requires attached evidence, FAIL means contrary evidence exists, and UNKNOWN means HOLD.

Three conclusions must remain distinct. A candidate design recommendation says which shape is worth pursuing. Classroom gate eligibility says the fictional evidence in this exercise satisfies the stated fictional gates. Real-world deployment authorization requires actual organizational, technical, legal, and operational evidence. No real-world authorization is granted anywhere in this artifact.

code.label: Hard-gate procedure
code.code:
1. Legal and data authority
2. Identity and access control
3. Critical safety and quality evaluation
4. Recovery and restoration
5. Capacity and service objectives
6. Preference scoring, but only among candidates that passed gates 1 through 5

PASS = sufficient scenario evidence is attached
FAIL = evidence contradicts the requirement
UNKNOWN = evidence is missing, so the result is HOLD

sections.title: Measure a fair comparison
paragraphs: Within one case, compare candidates with the exact same model revision and digest, runtime, adapter, request contract, safety policy, prompt distribution, input and output limits, offered load, timeout rule, warm-up policy, and failure accounting. Record hardware separately because deployment shapes can require different hardware. The comparisons in Cases A through D follow this rule within each case.

Do not treat measurements from different cases as fair performance comparisons. Cases A through D intentionally use different artifacts, context limits, concurrency, and outage conditions. Their results answer different requirements.

This guide chooses the nearest-rank percentile convention. Sort n successful latency observations in ascending order and take the observation at rank ceiling(0.95 x n). With five values [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] milliseconds, the rank is ceiling(4.75) = 5, so p95 is 50 milliseconds. With 20 observations, the nearest-rank p95 is observation 19. Timeouts are reported separately and cause a capacity failure rather than being silently removed.

The earlier common comparison used MODEL-CLASSROOM-7, digest sha256:SIMULATED, RUNTIME-CLASSROOM-2, ADAPTER-1, 2,048 input tokens, 256 output tokens, 20 requests per minute, and five offered concurrent slots. Its fictional p95 values were workstation 420 ms, container/on-premises 310 ms, edge 210 ms, and cloud-managed 260 ms. The workstation completed only two concurrent requests, so it failed the five-concurrent capacity condition. This low-load dataset cannot qualify Case B at 12 concurrent requests or Case D at 40 concurrent requests.

Evidence classification for this artifact is explicit: actual local observations supplied to the drafter: NONE. Fictional classroom observations: every latency, concurrency, memory, restore, outage, safety, identity, and cost value below. Unknown real deployment qualification: all four shapes in all four cases. Establish real qualification by reproducing the tests on the intended artifact, hardware, identity system, data path, operators, and failure conditions.

code.label: Measurement and evidence rules
code.code:
Nearest-rank p95:
  sort observations ascending
  rank = ceiling(0.95 * n)
  p95 = observation at that one-based rank

For n = 20:
  rank = ceiling(19) = 19

Fair only within a case:
  exact artifact + runtime + adapter + request contract + policy + load must match

Low-load exclusion:
  a five-concurrent run supplies no evidence that 12 or 40 concurrent requests pass

Evidence status:
  Actual local observations: NONE
  Fictional classroom observations: PRESENT
  Real deployment authorization: ABSENT

sections.title: Compare all four shapes without a blanket preference
paragraphs: The table identifies questions to test, not inherent winners. A deployment label cannot substitute for measured gates. For example, edge may be designed for disconnected use yet still fail because offline identity or rollback was not demonstrated. An on-premises candidate may keep data local yet fail because its measured capacity is too low. A managed candidate may reduce hardware work yet fail a facility-outage requirement.

Staffing is also evidence-dependent. One operator or a part-time operator is not declared inherently incapable. The gate fails only when the required coverage, response, restoration, or approval has not been demonstrated under the stated staffing arrangement.

code.label: Responsibility and qualification questions
code.code:
Shape               Useful property to test             Evidence still required
Workstation         Local operation for a small load      Exact concurrency, thermal behavior, access,
                                                          patching, backup, spare device, restore time

Container/on-prem   Shared service inside a facility     Host and image operation, explicit CPU/memory
                                                          limits, identity, capacity, backup, incidents

Edge               Device-local and disconnected use     Model fit, power duration, offline identity,
                                                          telemetry, update, physical access, rollback

Cloud-managed       Elastic service design and delegated Approved data path, identity, quota, evaluated
                    infrastructure tasks                 burst, cost, outage behavior, recovery

Eligibility rule:
  legal/data PASS + identity PASS + evaluation PASS + recovery PASS + capacity PASS
  otherwise FAIL or HOLD before preference scoring

sections.title: Four completed fictional workload decisions
paragraphs: All evidence in this section is simulated classroom evidence. It is not a provider benchmark, actual local observation, legal approval, or production authorization. Within each case, all candidates received the same exact request identity. The identities and contracts differ across cases, so cross-case latency comparisons are invalid.

Case A, private air-gapped lab. Requirement: one researcher, synthetic text, at most two concurrent requests, p95 at or below 700 ms, and restoration within four hours. Exact request identity: MODEL-A-CLASSROOM revision A7, digest sha256:SIM-A7, RUNTIME-A-2, ADAPTER-A1, policy SAFE-A1, 1,024 input tokens, 128 output tokens, two concurrent requests, 10 requests per minute, 2,000 ms timeout. The fictional license review recorded permission for this exact classroom artifact, synthetic-data authority passed, the named local researcher account passed identity, and 40 safety prompts produced zero critical failures against a zero-critical-failure threshold.

Case A result: workstation is both the classroom design recommendation and classroom gate-eligible. Its sorted latency observations were [410, 430, 445, 460, 475, 490, 510, 530, 590, 610] ms. With n=10, rank=ceiling(9.5)=10, so p95=610 ms. It completed two of two concurrent requests and restored a known-good image in a fictional 3 h 20 min drill, within the four-hour objective. Container/on-premises produced p95=520 ms from [330, 350, 370, 390, 410, 430, 450, 470, 500, 520], but its only simulated restore took 5 h 10 min because no facility-service operator was assigned, so recovery failed. Edge produced p95=480 ms from [290, 310, 330, 350, 370, 390, 410, 430, 460, 480], but its 6.4 GiB peak exceeded its 6.0 GiB memory available after OS reserve. Cloud-managed produced p95=410 ms while connected from [250, 270, 285, 300, 315, 330, 350, 370, 395, 410], but zero of 10 requests reached the service after the air gap was enabled. Thus low latency did not overcome hard failures.

Case B, confidential facility-local shared service. Requirement: 30 registered analysts, 12 peak concurrent requests, p95 at or below 1,000 ms, no external-network dependency, and restoration within 30 minutes. Exact request identity: MODEL-B-CLASSROOM revision B3, digest sha256:SIM-B3, RUNTIME-B-5, ADAPTER-B1, policy SAFE-B2, 2,048 input tokens, 256 output tokens, 12 concurrent requests, 48 requests per minute, 3,000 ms timeout. In this fictional scenario only, the exact artifact license was reviewed and recorded as permitting the simulated internal use. That is not a real license approval. The fictional data authority permitted confidential records only inside the facility boundary. Local identity tests mapped all 30 test accounts to accountable principals, denied all 10 unauthorized attempts, and retained audit records. A 120-prompt quality and safety suite had zero critical failures against a zero-critical-failure threshold.

Case B result: container/on-premises is the classroom design recommendation and classroom gate-eligible. Its sorted 12-concurrent latencies were [540, 555, 570, 585, 600, 615, 630, 645, 660, 675, 690, 705, 720, 735, 750, 765, 780, 795, 820, 840] ms. For n=20, rank 19 gives p95=820 ms. It completed all 240 requests in the simulated five-minute run without timeout. An image-host failure drill restored the known-good unit in 24 minutes using the named platform-team primary and backup, within the 30-minute objective. The run used explicit 8 CPU and 24 GiB container limits.

Case B alternatives failed concrete gates at the same request contract and 12-concurrent load. Workstation admitted two requests and timed out 10 of the first 12 at 3,000 ms, so it failed capacity. Edge admitted six requests and timed out six of the first 12; its 20 successful sorted observations were [860, 900, 930, 960, 990, 1020, 1060, 1100, 1140, 1180, 1220, 1260, 1300, 1340, 1380, 1420, 1460, 1500, 1560, 1620], giving p95=1,560 ms, above target. Its restore drill also took 47 minutes. Cloud-managed completed the connected test with sorted observations [420, 435, 450, 465, 480, 495, 510, 525, 540, 555, 570, 585, 600, 615, 630, 645, 660, 675, 700, 720], giving p95=700 ms, but 20 of 20 outage requests failed when the external path was removed. Therefore the common five-concurrent p95 of 310 ms was not used to qualify this 12-concurrent decision.

Case C, disconnected inspection device. Requirement: one field device must classify short maintenance notes through a six-hour network outage, with one concurrent request, p95 at or below 400 ms, and at least 20 percent memory headroom. Exact request identity: MODEL-C-CLASSROOM revision C4, digest sha256:SIM-C4, RUNTIME-C-3, ADAPTER-C1, policy SAFE-C1, 512 input tokens, 64 output tokens, one concurrent request, 12 requests per minute, 1,500 ms timeout. The fictional license and device-data authority passed. Offline device certificates accepted 20 valid requests and denied 10 invalid certificates. An 80-prompt safety and quality set had zero critical failures.

Case C result: edge is the classroom design recommendation and classroom gate-eligible. Device total RAM was 8.0 GiB, OS and fixed-service reserve was 2.0 GiB, and memory available to the model/runtime was therefore 6.0 GiB. Measured model/runtime peak was 4.8 GiB. Headroom used the available-memory denominator: (6.0 - 4.8) / 6.0 = 0.20, or exactly 20 percent. Sorted latency observations were [210, 220, 230, 240, 250, 260, 270, 280, 300, 320] ms, so n=10 gives p95=320 ms. A simulated battery run lasted 7 h 15 min, exceeding six hours. A signed rollback restored the previous artifact in 18 minutes, and post-restore identity, digest, and 10 smoke prompts passed.

Case C alternatives failed measured requirements. The workstation used the same artifact and produced p95=280 ms from [170, 180, 190, 200, 210, 220, 230, 240, 260, 280], but its simulated mobile power pack lasted 2 h 05 min, below six hours. Container/on-premises produced p95=240 ms from [145, 155, 165, 175, 185, 195, 205, 215, 230, 240] while connected, but zero of 10 device requests reached it after facility connectivity was removed. Cloud-managed produced p95=220 ms from [130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200, 210, 220] while connected, but zero of 10 outage requests reached it. These are power and connectivity failures, not shape stereotypes.

Case D, connected burst analysis. Requirement: 200 registered authorized users, not 200 simultaneous users. The measured planning peak is 40 concurrent requests, and the evaluated burst maximum is 60 concurrent requests for five minutes. Data is fictional non-confidential text, no offline operation is required, p95 must be at or below 1,200 ms at 40 concurrency and at or below 1,500 ms at the evaluated 60-concurrent burst, and restoration must complete within 30 minutes. Exact request identity: MODEL-D-CLASSROOM revision D9, digest sha256:SIM-D9, RUNTIME-D-6, ADAPTER-D1, policy SAFE-D3, 4,096 input tokens, 512 output tokens, 40 or 60 offered concurrent requests as specified, 240 requests per minute, 4,000 ms timeout.

Case D gate evidence: in this fictional scenario only, the exact MODEL-D-CLASSROOM revision D9 artifact license was reviewed and recorded as permitting the simulated managed use. This classroom fact is not a real license approval or production authorization. Fictional data authority approved this synthetic non-confidential dataset and approved the simulated managed region. Federated identity mapped all 200 test accounts to principals, enforced role checks, and denied 25 of 25 unauthorized requests. A 200-prompt quality and safety suite produced zero critical failures. Cloud-managed latency at 40 concurrency was [610, 625, 640, 655, 670, 685, 700, 715, 730, 745, 760, 775, 790, 805, 820, 835, 850, 865, 900, 930] ms, giving p95=900 ms. At the evaluated maximum burst of 60 concurrency it completed all 1,200 requests with zero timeout; sorted sampled latencies were [760, 780, 800, 820, 840, 860, 880, 900, 920, 940, 960, 980, 1000, 1020, 1040, 1060, 1080, 1120, 1180, 1240], giving p95=1,180 ms. A simulated regional-unit restoration to the known-good revision took 18 minutes and passed identity, digest, data-path, and 20 smoke-prompt checks.

Case D result: cloud-managed is classroom gate-eligible and is the classroom design recommendation. Container/on-premises admitted only 24 of 40 concurrent requests and timed out 16, then required 68 minutes in its restore drill. Workstation admitted two of 40 and timed out 38. Edge admitted eight of 40 and timed out 32. These alternatives fail measured capacity, and on-premises also fails recovery. The result does not claim that an unspecified real cloud service supports this workload. Real quota, contractual terms, artifact availability, region, identity path, pricing, and recovery remain UNKNOWN and therefore HOLD.

code.label: Classroom decisions and authorization boundary
code.code:
Case A
  Requirement: air-gapped, 2 concurrent, p95 <= 700 ms, restore <= 4 h
  Eligible recommendation: workstation
  Selected evidence: p95 610 ms, 2/2 concurrency, restore 3 h 20 min

Case B
  Requirement: facility-local, 12 concurrent, p95 <= 1,000 ms, restore <= 30 min
  Eligible recommendation: container/on-premises
  Selected evidence: p95 820 ms at 12 concurrency, restore 24 min

Case C
  Requirement: 6 h disconnected, p95 <= 400 ms, memory headroom >= 20%
  Eligible recommendation: edge
  Selected evidence: p95 320 ms, 7 h 15 min power, exactly 20% headroom, restore 18 min

Case D
  Requirement: 200 registered users, peak 40 concurrent, evaluated burst 60
  Eligible recommendation: cloud-managed
  Selected evidence: p95 900 ms at 40, p95 1,180 ms at 60, restore 18 min

All values above: FICTIONAL CLASSROOM OBSERVATIONS
Actual local measurements: NONE
Real-world authorization: ABSENT for A, B, C, and D

sections.title: Use explicit fictional cost and preference arithmetic
paragraphs: The following values preserve the original fictional 12-month Case B cost comparison. They are not current prices, provider measurements, or procurement quotes. One-time and monthly costs are kept separate. Unless expressly listed, the model excludes labor, tax, hardware depreciation after the planning horizon, financing, API-token charges, data transfer, and contingency.

Workstation cost is $2,400 one-time plus $150 per month for electricity, backup storage, and support: $2,400 + 12 x $150 = $4,200. Container/on-premises cost is $18,000 one-time for two servers and networking plus $2,200 per month for facility power, backup, monitoring, and support: $18,000 + 12 x $2,200 = $44,400. Edge cost is $9,000 one-time for three devices and staging equipment plus $1,100 per month for fleet support: $9,000 + 12 x $1,100 = $22,200. Cloud-managed cost is $0 one-time in this classroom model plus $6,800 per month for fictional service, storage, and support charges: 12 x $6,800 = $81,600.

Preference scoring applies only to candidates that passed all hard gates for the case. For the eligible Case B on-premises candidate, locality contributes 5 x 0.30 = 1.50, latency contributes 4 x 0.20 = 0.80, staffing contributes 3 x 0.15 = 0.45, support contributes 3 x 0.15 = 0.45, and cost contributes 2 x 0.20 = 0.40. The total is 3.60 out of 5. The staffing score describes the fictional baseline team and excludes labor cost from the TCO. It is not evidence that staffing or recovery passes after staffing changes.

A candidate with a higher preference score remains ineligible when any hard gate is FAIL or UNKNOWN. Cost and preference arithmetic cannot override legal, identity, evaluation, recovery, capacity, locality, or outage requirements.

code.label: Fictional costs and preserved weighted score
code.code:
Candidate          One-time   Monthly   Fictional 12-month total
Workstation        $2,400     $150      $4,200
Container/on-prem  $18,000    $2,200    $44,400
Edge               $9,000     $1,100    $22,200
Cloud-managed      $0         $6,800    $81,600

Eligible Case B on-premises preference score:
  locality: 5 * 0.30 = 1.50
  latency:  4 * 0.20 = 0.80
  staffing: 3 * 0.15 = 0.45
  support:  3 * 0.15 = 0.45
  cost:     2 * 0.20 = 0.40
  total:                  3.60 / 5

Labor is excluded from these fictional cost totals.

sections.title: Verify artifacts, runtimes, safety, and recovery
paragraphs: A model-family repository is only a discovery point. It does not prove permission for a particular artifact, context capacity, runtime compatibility, safety, quality, hardware fit, or deployment availability. Four official discovery repositories are Qwen at https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3, Meta Llama materials at https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models, Mistral materials at https://github.com/mistralai/cookbook, and Microsoft Phi materials at https://github.com/microsoft/PhiCookBook. No further capability or approval claim is made from these links.

For the exact artifact, record its name, immutable revision, digest, license text, tokenizer, adapter, runtime, supported hardware, and organizational approval. A fictional statement that Case B's license was verified means only that the classroom scenario supplied a passing gate. It is not evidence that MODEL-B-CLASSROOM exists or that any real model license has been approved.

Safety and quality evidence must bind to the exact build and acceptance threshold. Recovery evidence must exercise admission stopping, in-flight reconciliation, restoration of the known-good serving unit, artifact and configuration verification, identity checks, data-boundary checks, and post-restore safety or quality checks. A configured backup, replica, deployment controller, or rollback button is not equivalent to a tested restore.

Unknown deployment qualification must be recorded without softening. Examples include: exact real artifact permission UNKNOWN, establish through official license text and authorized legal review; real edge memory fit UNKNOWN, establish using a representative build and peak-memory measurement; real cloud quota and pricing UNKNOWN, establish from dated first-party terms or a quote; real operator coverage UNKNOWN, establish through an approved coverage plan and exercise. Every such UNKNOWN produces HOLD.

code.label: Minimum real evidence bundle
code.code:
Artifact: exact name, revision, digest, license, tokenizer, adapter, runtime
Data: classification, authority, locations, retention, deletion, transfer path
Identity: principals, authentication, authorization, secrets, audit trail, offline behavior
Evaluation: representative quality set, safety set, thresholds, critical failures
Load: exact request contract, concurrency, rate, p95 rule, errors, saturation, ceilings
Memory/power: total, reserves, measured peak, denominator, duration and conditions
Recovery: failure injected, admission stopped, restore performed, postconditions, elapsed time
Operations: named owners, coverage, patching, telemetry, update, rollback, support
Cost: dated one-time and recurring inputs, labor treatment, exclusions
Decision: gate outcomes, evidence links, recommendation, authorization, expiry, triggers

sections.title: Completed classroom decision record for Case B
paragraphs: This completed record corrects the prior contradiction between a 12-concurrent requirement and a five-concurrent test. It uses the Case B 12-concurrent run. It also records the exact artifact permission as verified only inside the fictional scenario rather than UNKNOWN. These facts make the candidate classroom gate-eligible, but they do not authorize a real deployment.

Decision vocabulary: classroom design recommendation means container/on-premises is the preferred design to pursue; classroom gate eligibility means all fictional Case B gates have supporting simulated evidence; real-world deployment authorization is absent because no actual local evidence or organizational approval was supplied.

sections.title: Independent changed requirement
paragraphs: Independent learner task: reassess Case B while keeping its exact model, digest, runtime, adapter, data classification, 30 registered analysts, 12-concurrent peak, request limits, safety threshold, p95 target, and 30-minute restoration objective unchanged. Change only two declared facts: the platform staffing arrangement becomes one part-time operator with no backup, and the required outage becomes a 12-hour facility-network outage rather than merely an external-network outage.

The baseline 24-minute restoration drill still occurred. Do not say that there was never a tested restore. Instead, decide whether it remains applicable. The baseline drill used the original primary-and-backup platform team, the functioning facility network, and the online local identity path. The changed case removes that staffing arrangement and removes the facility network for 12 hours. Therefore the old drill does not establish recovery ownership, offline identity, service reachability, or restoration under the changed conditions.

For each of workstation, container/on-premises, edge, and cloud-managed, report the changed hard-gate result and the concrete evidence needed to reopen it. Do not infer that one part-time operator is inherently incapable. Ask whether required coverage and restoration have been demonstrated with that declared owner. Do not use weighted scores until a candidate passes every changed hard gate.

code.label: Facts held constant and facts changed
code.code:
Held constant:
  MODEL-B-CLASSROOM B3, sha256:SIM-B3
  RUNTIME-B-5, ADAPTER-B1, SAFE-B2
  confidential facility-controlled data
  30 registered analysts, 12 peak concurrency
  2,048 input / 256 output tokens
  p95 <= 1,000 ms
  restore <= 30 minutes

Changed only:
  staffing: original primary plus backup -> one part-time operator, no backup
  outage: external-network outage -> 12-hour facility-network outage

Baseline restore fact:
  24-minute drill occurred, but under the original team, network and identity conditions.
  Its applicability to the changed case is not demonstrated.

sections.title: Complete answer to the changed task
paragraphs: Result: HOLD. No candidate is classroom gate-eligible from the available changed-case evidence. This is not a conclusion that every shape is technically impossible. It means none has demonstrated all required gates under the new staffing arrangement and 12-hour facility-network outage.

Workstation: FAIL on demonstrated capacity because the unchanged Case B test admitted only two of 12 concurrent requests and timed out 10. Recovery is also UNKNOWN for the changed conditions because no workstation restoration exercise used the part-time owner during the 12-hour facility-network outage. Reopen only after a 12-concurrent representative test passes, an approved confidential-data and offline-identity design exists, and the declared owner completes a restoration within 30 minutes under the changed outage.

Container/on-premises: its baseline 12-concurrent p95 of 820 ms remains valid capacity evidence for the original network condition, but recovery and identity become UNKNOWN for the changed condition. The 24-minute drill depended on the original primary-and-backup team, functioning facility network, and online local identity path. It does not demonstrate who notices, authorizes, performs, or verifies recovery when the only declared operator is unavailable, nor does it show request identity during a facility-network outage. Reopen by approving an offline identity and audit path, naming demonstrated coverage for the recovery objective, and repeating the restore, 12-concurrent load, and post-restore checks during a representative facility-network outage.

Edge: disconnected operation is a plausible design property, but this Case B edge candidate already failed baseline capacity by admitting six of 12 requests, had p95 1,560 ms against the 1,000 ms target, and restored in 47 minutes against the 30-minute objective. There is also no changed-case evidence for confidential-data synchronization, offline identity for 30 analysts, centralized auditing, or recovery coverage. Reopen only after a redesigned edge service passes 12-concurrent latency, confidential-data, offline-identity, audit, update, and sub-30-minute recovery tests under the changed owner arrangement.

Cloud-managed: the baseline connected p95 of 700 ms does not qualify a 12-hour facility-network outage. In the supplied fictional outage test, 20 of 20 requests failed when only the external path was removed. A facility-network outage is at least as different from the connected test and also interrupts the demonstrated local identity and request paths. Reopen only with an approved independent connectivity path, approved confidential-data routing, identity and audit continuity, a 12-concurrent outage load test, and a restoration exercise under the declared staffing arrangement.

Preference scores and the fictional costs are non-decisive because no candidate passes every changed hard gate. Real-world authorization remains absent even if future classroom evidence makes one candidate eligible.

sections.title: Causal grading feedback for the changed task
paragraphs: Full credit identifies exactly two changed inputs: staffing and the outage boundary. It preserves the factual baseline 24-minute restore drill but explains why that evidence no longer establishes the changed recovery gate. The causal chain is: changed owner and network conditions invalidate applicability of the previous recovery and identity demonstration; UNKNOWN therefore produces HOLD. Full credit also retains the concrete pre-existing capacity failures for workstation and edge and the outage failure for cloud-managed.

A strong answer distinguishes possibility from evidence. It may say that container/on-premises, edge, or another architecture could be redesigned, but it must not call the candidate eligible until recovery coverage, offline identity, exact 12-concurrent capacity, data authority, and restoration are demonstrated under the changed conditions.

Partial credit identifies the facility outage but selects edge merely because edge commonly supports intermittent connectivity. That ignores the measured six-of-12 admission result, p95 of 1,560 ms, 47-minute restoration, and missing offline identity evidence. Partial credit also applies when an answer selects cloud-managed merely because infrastructure operation is delegated, while ignoring the 20-of-20 outage failure and the customer's identity, data, and recovery obligations.

Partial credit identifies staffing as a concern but states that one part-time operator is inherently incapable. The correct causal finding is narrower: required coverage and recovery have not been demonstrated with the declared staffing arrangement. Evidence could change that result.

No credit claims that the baseline had no tested restore, because a fictional 24-minute drill was recorded. No credit also keeps the original recommendation without reassessment, treats UNKNOWN as PASS, uses the five-concurrent 310 ms dataset to qualify 12 concurrency, allows a preference score to override a hard gate, or presents classroom simulations as actual measurements.

The general diagnosis is evidence mismatch: a fact supports a gate only when it matches the exact artifact, requirement, load, environment, and operating conditions being decided. A five-concurrent latency result cannot establish a 12-concurrent capacity requirement. Missing exact-artifact permission remains UNKNOWN and causes HOLD rather than PASS. A recorded restore drill must be preserved as historical evidence, but it does not establish recovery after the owner, network, or identity conditions change. Memory qualification requires measured peak use and an explicit headroom denominator, while burst qualification requires a representative run at the stated burst load with latency, completion, and timeout results. Applying these checks keeps fictional classroom eligibility separate from actual local observation and real deployment authorization.

code.label: Grading checkpoints
code.code:
Full credit:
  identifies only the two declared changes
  preserves the historical 24-minute baseline drill
  explains why baseline evidence is inapplicable to the changed conditions
  reports no eligible candidate and returns HOLD
  gives candidate-specific measurements and reopen actions
  separates classroom eligibility from real authorization

Partial credit:
  notices outage or staffing but relies on deployment-label stereotypes
  calls staffing impossible instead of identifying missing demonstrated coverage
  omits one or more candidate-specific failed gates

No credit:
  says no baseline restore ever occurred
  treats UNKNOWN as PASS
  uses five-concurrent data for a 12-concurrent gate
  overrides a hard gate with cost or weighted score
  reports fictional values as actual observations
